service.description: The parameters every OMS order-grain extract takes (an interface: extract#HotWaxOmsGqlOrders, extract#HotWaxOmsGqlProducts implement it). Writes normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-orders-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection: top-level record fields to keep in the output file. When present, each order is trimmed to these fields after reconciliation filtering and before writing (callers compute the list from the rule set's join-key and rule fields plus the display fields). Absent means full untrimmed records (backward compatible).

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules. Each rule names a top-level record field and a comma-separated list of exact values; matching orders are dropped before the extract file is written and counted per rule in requestMetadata.filters.configuredExclusions. Absent or empty means no configured exclusions (backward compatible).

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id. On its own it is enough for the extractor to heartbeat a running order count onto the run's RUNNING extract step as pages are consumed, so the live view can show the count climbing. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Required for progress to land, because the heartbeat targets the RUNNING step for this stage and the same extractor runs on either side depending on the saved run's source order. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2 for callers that predate this parameter.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count — typically the other side's extracted record count for the same window. Only the second extract of a run can supply one; the first has nothing finished to divide against.

parameter.name: exchangeManifestFileLocation
parameter.description: Location of the exchange-manifest sidecar written when the window contained excluded exchange orders; null otherwise. Identities/amounts only, capped at 500 entries.

service.description: Extract HotWax OMS sales orders at ORDER grain over the GraphQL endpoint (/rest/s1/graphql), pages from OmsGqlOrderPageSource shaped by OmsExtractSupport (exclusions, filters, projection). Adds hasPaymentPreference / paymentMethodTypeIds for the presence OPP rule (DAR-BE-064). A DISTINCT service name is required: the connector registry resolves rows by it.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-120. Read only these orders by orderId, whatever their date, instead of the window: a conclusion lookup. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: orderId, or externalId (the Shopify order id; DAR-BE-156, a Shopify-paired audit check's re-check).

parameter.name: conclusionLookup
parameter.description: DAR-BE-205. With lookupKeys: this read answers a conclusion lookup, so exchange orders come back too (the exchange exclusion is for a sales-order comparison). An audit re-check by key leaves it off and keeps the exclusion.

service.description: DAR-BE-157. Every sellable HotWax product (not virtual, FINISHED_GOOD or MARKETING_PKG_PICK, not discontinued) over the GraphQL endpoint, one record per product keyed by nsKey: its NETSUITE_PRODUCT_ID (the NetSuite item internal id), HOTWAX-ONLY:productId when it has none, DUPLICATE:id:productId for every product after the first sharing one. Not windowed: windowStart/windowEnd are accepted and ignored (requestMetadata.windowIgnored). A DISTINCT service name is required: the connector registry resolves rows by it.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-186. Read only these products by productId, whatever their state, each with its NETSUITE_PRODUCT_ID or none (the conclusion brain's productNetsuiteId question), instead of the catalogue. A product HotWax does not have is absent. Source filters do not apply.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: productId.

service.description: The parameters every OMS returns extract takes (an interface: extract#HotWaxOmsGqlReturns implements it). Writes normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier: the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as order extraction.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds. The half-open lower bound on entryDate.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats. Exclusive upper bound on entryDate, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-returns-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection of top-level record fields. items[] is always retained regardless of this list, because the nested-line contract (RQ-21) does not survive a projection that names only header fields.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as the order extractors. These run client-side: the endpoint has no knowledge of tenant exclusion rules. The expected rule here excludes returns whose returnChannelEnumId never has a Shopify counterpart.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for progress heartbeats. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count.

service.description: Extract HotWax OMS returns for an automation window over the OMS GraphQL API (connector OMS_RETURNS_GQL, DAR-BE-040 fix 3), writing a {records, metadata} file. GraphQL `returns` carries every return, pending ones included. It excludes returns with no Shopify reference (counted as excludedNoShopifyRefCount) and, by default, RETURN_CANCELLED (excludedCancelledCount), which the Shopify side suppresses (DAR-BE-027). Needs the OMS GraphQL upgrade (gorjana 2026-09-30); on an OMS without it the extract FAILS rather than returning an empty file.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-119. Read only these records by key (returnId), whatever their date, instead of the window: an audit re-checking its older open findings. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: returnId.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds. Sent as the half-open lower bound on entryDate.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats. Exclusive upper bound on entryDate, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-returns-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as the order extractors. These run client-side, after the built-in exclusions. The expected rule here excludes returns whose returnChannelEnumId never has a Shopify counterpart.

parameter.name: includeReturnsWithoutShopifyRef
parameter.description: DAR-BE-094. Keep the returns with no Shopify reference (counted as keptNoShopifyRefCount) instead of excluding them: the OMS's own Happiness Guarantee and sellable returns, which Shopify never sees but NetSuite must. For a check against NetSuite (R8), set in the automation source's safeMetadataJson.parameters; every Shopify comparison leaves it off.

parameter.name: withReturnCredit
parameter.description: DAR-BE-192. Also read the payments each return's responses refund and write the credit HotWax gives the return as returnCredit (each refunded payment once, summed; 0 when none), for a check that its NetSuite credit memo carries it. One more lookup a page, so off unless a run side sets it.

parameter.name: onlyCancelledReturns
parameter.description: DAR-BE-094 R16. Read ONLY the returns the OMS cancelled (asked of the OMS by status), with or without a Shopify reference: for a check that nothing stays open in NetSuite for them. Set in the automation source's safeMetadataJson.parameters.

service.description:
The parameters every OMS unit-grain order extract takes (an interface: extract#HotWaxOmsGqlOrderItems implements it): ONE RECORD PER UNIT, written as normalized JSON to the automation data-manager folder.
WHY UNITS AND NOT LINES: OMS explodes a Shopify line of quantity N into N single-unit OrderItems for routing, and the Spark compare core is a left_anti join followed by .distinct() - set semantics. At line grain a line OMS imported SHORT still matches a complete Shopify line, so the pair reports clean on exactly the defect it exists to find. Each record therefore carries a unitOrdinal.
NO keepRecordFields: the unit record IS the projection. Passing an order-shaped field list would strip every field a unit record has and still report a successful extract.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier: the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as sales-order extraction.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats as windowStart.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: Only orderDate (or empty), what the Shopify side's created_at window matches. Any other field is refused rather than ignored (DAR-BE-038 skew).

parameter.name: orderStatusIds
parameter.description: Declared so a caller passing it is refused (the GraphQL order read cannot filter by status) rather than silently widened.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as extract#HotWaxOmsOrders. Applied to ORDERS before flattening, because the exchange scan needs the full record.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for progress heartbeats. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count.

parameter.name: recordCount
parameter.description: Number of UNITS written, not orders.

parameter.name: requestMetadata
parameter.description: Carries droppedNullLineIdCount and nonUnitQuantityCount beside the usual filter counts. Those two record units the extract could not key and therefore LOST, which is a different thing from a record a filter excluded on purpose.

service.description:
DAR-BE-116. OMS order items over GraphQL (every OMS read goes through GraphQL): ONE RECORD PER UNIT through OmsOrderLineUnitSupport's flattener, with two deliberate differences from the Shopify-side line units (exchange exclusion OFF, items without a Shopify id KEPT). Orders are read with their ship groups, the items by orderId in batches, each placed under its ship group; a multi-day window runs as parallel day slices on the endpoint's one cost bucket. A distinct service name because the connector registry resolves a connector row by its extract service name; this one is gated on the OMS_ORDER_ITEMS_GQL endpoint.
NOT carried: salesChannelEnumId, which gorjana's GraphQL Order type does not have (SDL 2026-10-23). A source filter on it is refused rather than ignored.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-119. Read only these records by key (omsOrderId (the OMS orderId)), whatever their date, instead of the window: an audit re-checking its older open findings. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: omsOrderId (the OMS orderId).

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier; the same credential and baseUrl answer /rest/s1/graphql.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: Only orderDate (or empty): the GraphQL order extract windows on orderDate and refuses any other field rather than widening the extract.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional include/exclude rules evaluated per UNIT, as on extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems. A rule on a field the GraphQL unit does not carry (salesChannelEnumId) fails the extract.

parameter.name: requestMetadata
parameter.description: As extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems: keptNullShopifyIdCount, droppedNullLineIdCount and nonUnitQuantityCount beside the usual filter counts, plus the GraphQL pagination (sliceCount, pageCount, lookupCalls).

service.description: Point lookup of OMS order groups by Shopify externalId for the exchange pair verify stage, over GraphQL (DAR-BE-129), any date. A failed lookup returns ok=false with an empty map — it never classifies anything.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant; when present, config access is checked against it instead of a user-session active tenant.

service.description: Order lines OMS booked a return against, keyed by the originating Shopify order id, over GraphQL (DAR-BE-085, DAR-BE-086). The returns verify stage pairs a missing-in-OMS Shopify event by order and line when no shared id can exist: AfterShip warranty returns (keyed WARRANTY-uuid in OMS) and returns on Shopify orders older than the 60-day read limit (rebuilt without a refund id). Cancelled returns are left out. A failed lookup returns ok=false with an empty map; it never pairs anything.

parameter.name: externalIds
parameter.description: Shopify order ids (OMS OrderHeader.externalId).

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant; when present, config access is checked against it instead of a user-session active tenant.

service.description: DAR-BE-111. Each order's HotWax statusId by OMS order id, over GraphQL: the NetSuite orders an audit check found never shipped and never billed, asked of HotWax (completed or cancelled there is a finding). Ids are asked in chunks and every answer is echo-checked. A failed lookup returns ok=false with nothing classified; it never calls an order missing.

parameter.name: orderIds
parameter.description: OMS order ids (NetSuite custbody_hc_order_id).

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant; when present, config access is checked against it instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: withItems
parameter.description: DAR-BE-190. Ask each order's items instead of the order: itemStatusByKey is filled and statusByOrderId stays empty; missingIds are the orders HotWax returned no item for.

parameter.name: statusByOrderId
parameter.description: OMS order id -> statusId.

parameter.name: itemStatusByKey
parameter.description: DAR-BE-190, withItems: "orderId|orderItemSeqId" -> the item's statusId.

parameter.name: missingIds
parameter.description: Ids HotWax has no order for.

service.description:
Point-existence check for OMS return ids over GraphQL, the missing-in-OMS mirror of Shopify's lookup#ShopifyRefundOrReturnIds. The saved-run verification pass calls this to confirm or refute "missing in OMS" differences.
Escapes the run window by construction: OMS windows on entryDate (when a return was CREATED) while the Shopify side windows on the event createdAt (when it was REFUNDED), so a return opened weeks before its refund sits inside one window and far outside the other. Measured 2026-08-20, that mismatch explained 45 of 59 remaining differences, median age 11 days.
Three passes: returns by returnId, by externalId (the Shopify refund id), then returnIdentifications(idValue:) for the Shopify return id. Ids are checked in batches and every returned record is echo-checked against the ids actually requested. Ids a pass cannot check come back in unresolvedIds — unchecked, never confirmed missing.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier.

parameter.name: externalIds
parameter.description: Shopify refund or return ids as they appear in the OMS externalId field.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.
